summary: Bidirectional alignment fails. Core writer-fencing, sticky pins, sync_standby, cutover/epoch, capture idempotency, healthz/readyz split, and failover-status schema are largely grounded in instruction.md plus runbook.md and mostly covered by tests, but four material phantoms remain, runbook readiness/accepting_checkout conjunctions are only partially graded, instruction vs runbook vs readiness_policy disagree on the /readyz gate set, and solver-visible Python modules contain a material Defect/Starter repair map. Instruction shape is within limits and the delegated runbook is legitimate ops documentation; these defects still require REVISE before Quality Interlock can pass.

evidence.observation: Two short paragraphs: incident symptoms (place double-write, OPEN after pay, dual captures for att-inc-20001/20007/20012), paths under /app/ha, preserve manage.py and checkout/health/ready routes, writer-only checkout writes, no lagged standby for recent writers, sticky keys not in django_session (pins alias), one attempt_id one capture, /readyz 503 for dual-writable / seq gap past max_lag_lsn / old writer still allowed, dump /app/ha/out/failover-status.json per runbook object.

Delegated ops contract: sync_standby/cutover/dump_failover, fence lease semantics, sticky pins key/alias, lag formula vs max_lag_lsn, /healthz vs /readyz (one writer, seq budget, pins reachable, no repeat captures), failover-status.json schema, accepting_checkout true only for single writer + repeat_captures=0 + standby_only_orders=0 + seq in budget + incident orders on standby + standby lease not writable.

Shift note restates AZ-B writer, place-on-replica, OPEN confirmation, dual captures, half-finished sync with writable lease on standby; asks not to rebuild schema or rename checkout URLs; /readyz must mean safe for cards.
Supports current-state claims: az-a still writable, place on replica, sticky miss in django_session, capture twice for the three attempt ids, sync cutoff and fence copy, healthz/readyz collapsed.

36 pytest behaviors: F2P writer/standby isolation, sticky/pins, lag/seq_gap, sync_standby, cutover/epoch, capture/reservation idempotency variants, readyz/healthz, dump schema/split/repeat_captures, reconnect; P2P healthz/runbook strings/manage+routes/20k orders/blank attempt/max_lag_lsn key presence.
compute_accepting_checkout also requires pins=='shared' and fence_copied_to_standby==False; pins enum shared/local/missing. Runbook accepting_checkout paragraph omits the pins==shared clause.

evaluate_readiness gates on writer count, seq gap, pins_shared+reachable, repeat_captures, standby_only_orders, fence_copied_to_standby, and incident_orders_on_standby — broader than instruction's three /readyz triggers and broader than the runbook /readyz sentence.
Module docstring and inline comments diagnose starter AZ-B→replica write divert explicitly.
Docstring and '# Defect:' comment diagnose name-match fencing without writable+epoch invalidation.
'# Defect:' comment states pins land in DB session + default locmem, not shared pins alias.
Docstring diagnoses hardcoded cutoff and copying fence leases.
Docstring and '# Defect:' comment diagnose row-count gap treated as lag budget.
Docstring states starter always inserts another side-effect row.
Module docstring names leftover AZ-B affinity mis-applied in controlplane.router; later comment marks defect-facing affinity branch.
Public config exposes sticky_seconds=5, max_lag_lsn=25, incident_min_order_id=19980 used by lag/sticky/incident-window semantics.

Any material phantom test, untested material requirement, grading-relevant ambiguity, or material implementation-diagnosis leakage requires REVISE; PASS needs exhaustive walk with empty BLOCKING_FINDING_IDS.
Instruction owns the engineering ask; docs may hold schemas/runbooks; solver-visible material must not become a repair map or module-level defect diagnosis.

findings.criterion: Solver-visible material must not reveal the repair plan or diagnose which modules/behaviors are incomplete or buggy.
findings.why_it_matters: Across the HA controlplane and fulfill packages, module docstrings and inline comments explicitly label Starter/Defect behavior (AZ-B writes to replica, name-only fencing, pins in django_session, row-count lag, always-insert captures, fence copy on sync, optimistic dump, collapsed readyz). That is a module-level repair map aligned with the F2P suite and collapses specialized inference into following author annotations.
findings.minimal_remediation: Environment/Instruction Writer: remove Defect/Starter diagnosis narration from solver-visible sources. Keep realistic broken behavior without naming which branch/module is wrong or how it misbehaves. Re-freeze and re-run Q4.
findings.regression_risk: Low if only comments/docstrings are cleaned; do not weaken behavioral verifier assertions that catch those defects.

findings.criterion: Every substantive verifier behavior must be discoverable from the solver-visible contract.
findings.why_it_matters: The test requires pay to fail when order.write_lsn is ahead of primary wal_lsn. Instruction and runbook discuss writer fencing, sticky reads, replica lag for read eligibility, and one capture per attempt_id — not a pay-time write_lsn vs wal_lsn commit fence. A contract-faithful fix can omit that gate and still fail grading.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: drop or rewrite the assertion to a discoverable invariant. Or Q1/Q3: state the pay/capture commit-fence rule in instruction or runbook if it is intentional.
findings.regression_risk: Low if removed or documented; medium if documenting invents a new safety rule not needed for the incident.

findings.criterion: Every substantive verifier behavior must be discoverable from the solver-visible contract.
findings.why_it_matters: Empty attempt_id rejection via CheckoutError is graded but never stated in the ticket or runbook. Preserving or adding that validation is an unstated API rule.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: remove the blank-attempt assertion, or Q1/Q3: document that empty attempt_id must be rejected on the public place path.

findings.criterion: Preservation/P2P tests need discoverable preservation intent; exact seed cardinalities are not free-floating requirements.
findings.why_it_matters: The verifier requires primary Order count == 20000. Solver-visible material says leave manage.py/routes and do not rebuild schema/rename URLs — not that the seeded order book volume is an acceptance invariant. A correct fencing/idempotency fix that archives or trims rows fails grading.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: replace exact 20000 with schema/route preservation or a weaker non-destructive check. Or Q1: state that operational order history volume must remain intact if that is truly required.
findings.regression_risk: Low if swapped for schema/route/API preservation already stated.

findings.criterion: Tests must not grade a different idempotency surface than the stated contract.
evidence_refs: django-checkout-failover-ha/instruction.md: one attempt_id gets one capture effect
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires one capture effect per attempt_id (covered by dedicated capture tests). test_f2p_pay_twice_one_commit instead requires exactly one COMMITTED reservation after double pay — a distinct inventory invariant never stated in instruction or runbook.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: drop the reservation-count assertion or fold it into capture-only checks already contracted. Or Q1/Q3: state pay idempotency for reservation commit if intentional.
findings.regression_risk: Low if removed; keep capture exactly-once coverage.

findings.criterion: Every material solver-visible requirement that should be graded must have meaningful behavioral coverage.
findings.why_it_matters: Runbook defines /readyz readiness as one writer, seq gap inside budget, pins reachable, and no repeat capture rows. Verifier only forces non-200 for dual writable leases and unsafe seq gap. Pins-unreachable and repeat-captures>0 can leave /readyz green while violating the delegated contract.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: add behavioral /readyz cases for unreachable/non-shared pins and repeat_captures>0. Coordinate with Q3 if instruction/runbook gate sets are intentionally different.
findings.regression_risk: Medium; exercise HTTP /readyz outcomes without locking private helper names.

findings.criterion: Documented accepting_checkout conjunction in the dump contract must be meaningfully graded.
findings.why_it_matters: Runbook requires accepting_checkout true only when single writer, repeat_captures=0, standby_only_orders=0, seq gap in budget, incident-window orders on standby, and standby lease not writable. Tests only show accepting_checkout false under split writers or seeded repeat_captures. standby_only_orders, incident_orders_on_standby, fence/standby-writable, and seq-budget dimensions of the dump field are unasserted, so incorrect dump logic can pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: add independent dump cases flipping each accepting_checkout conjunct (false when violated; optionally one true happy path after sync/cutover/cleanup). Do not embed a callable end-to-end oracle.
findings.regression_risk: Medium; keep assertions on public dump fields, not private compute helpers.

findings.criterion: Grading-relevant ambiguity about authority, failure handling, or readiness gates requires REVISE.
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction lists three /readyz 503 triggers (dual writable, seq gap past max_lag_lsn, old writer still allowed). Runbook adds pins reachable and no repeat captures. readiness_policy also fails readiness for standby_only_orders, fence_copied_to_standby, and missing incident replay. A solver cannot know which set determines HTTP 503 vs dump-only accepting_checkout, changing accepted behavior.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q3: make one authoritative readiness gate list in instruction and/or runbook, and clarify which gates apply to live /readyz versus dump accepting_checkout. Align readiness_policy and tests to that list.
findings.regression_risk: Medium; clarifying may require Q2 test updates so HTTP and dump assertions match the published set.

findings.criterion: Stable dump semantics for accepting_checkout should not silently diverge between runbook text and schema helpers.
findings.why_it_matters: Runbook omits pins=='shared' from the accepting_checkout conjunction; status_schema requires it. Until tests demand accepting true, this is less pass/fail decisive, but it still muddies the public dump contract.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q3: add pins shared to the runbook accepting_checkout sentence, or remove the pins clause from compute_accepting_checkout if not intended. Then ensure Q2 coverage matches.

findings.criterion: P2P cases should meaningfully preserve claimed behavior rather than only key presence.
findings.why_it_matters: Docstring claims desk config/runbook name the seq-gap budget used for replica eligibility, but the body only asserts max_lag_lsn exists and is >=0. It does not prove tiny-lag hiding or eligibility flipping at the budget boundary (partially covered elsewhere by idle-read/sync tests).
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: rename/docstring align, or add a thin budget-boundary eligibility assertion if not redundant with existing lag tests.

findings.criterion: Optional duration semantics in the runbook should be graded or treated as non-normative.
findings.why_it_matters: Runbook says post-write reads stay on the writer for sticky_seconds. Tests prove sticky routing and pin-store durability but never expiry after sticky_seconds. Advisory under-test; not currently a phantom.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: add a TTL expiry case, or Q3: mark sticky_seconds as configuration detail without a hard graded TTL if expiry is not required.
findings.regression_risk: Low to medium if adding time-based tests; prefer deterministic clock/TTL hooks over wall sleeps.
